links.reason: John speaks of “the one and only Son from the Father”; Genesis has God say “your only son Isaac, whom you love.”
John speaks of “the angels of God ascending and descending”; Genesis tells of Jacob’s dream, where “God’s angels were going up and down.”
John says “Not one of His bones will be broken”; Exodus says of the meat, “you may not break any of the bones.”
John says “He gave them bread from heaven to eat”; Exodus has the LORD say “I will rain down bread from heaven for you.”
John says “Not one of His bones will be broken”; Numbers says of the Passover meal that they may not “break any of its bones.”
John says people expect the Christ “from the line of David”; 2 Samuel promises “I will raise up your descendant after you.”
John repeats “They divided My garments among them, and cast lots for My clothing”; Psalms 22:18 has the same words in the present tense.
John says “Not one of His bones will be broken”; Psalms says “He protects all his bones; not one of them will be broken.”
John says “They hated Me without reason”; Psalms 35:19 speaks of “those who hate me without reason.”
John repeats “The one who shares My bread has lifted up his heel”; Psalms has “the one who shared my bread.”
John says “They hated Me without reason”; Psalms 69:4 says “Those who hate me without cause outnumber the hairs of my head.”
John has “Zeal for Your house will consume Me”; Psalms 69:9 has “zeal for Your house has consumed me.”
John has Jesus say “I am thirsty”; Psalms 69:21 says “gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.”
John says “sour wine” was lifted to His mouth on a sponge; Psalms 69:21 says “gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.”
John says “He gave them bread from heaven to eat”; Psalms 78:24 says “He gave them grain from heaven.”
John repeats “I have said you are gods”; Psalms 82:6 has “You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.”
John says the Christ “will remain forever”; Psalms 89:36 says “his offspring shall endure forever.”
John says they shouted “Hosanna!” as they went out to meet Him; Psalms asks, “O LORD, save us, we pray”.
John has “Streams of living water will flow from within him”; Proverbs says “The words of a man’s mouth are deep waters”.
John repeats Isaiah: “understand with their hearts, and turn”, then “I would heal them” where Isaiah says “be healed”.
John repeats Isaiah: “voice of one calling”; John has “Make straight the way for the Lord”, Isaiah has “Prepare the way for the LORD”.
John has “Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion”; Isaiah tells Zion “do not be afraid” and says “Here is your God”.
John repeats Isaiah’s questions “Who has believed our message?” and “to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?”
John repeats Isaiah’s words that people “will be taught by” God; Isaiah says it of “all your sons.”
John says “they will all be taught by God”; Jeremiah says “I will put My law in their minds.”
John says “they will all be taught by God”; Jeremiah says no man will teach his neighbor, because “they will all know Me.”
John says the Christ will “come from” Bethlehem; Micah says out of “Bethlehem Ephrathah” will “come forth” One to be ruler over Israel.
John repeats Zechariah’s words “O Daughter of Zion” and “your King,” and says the King sits on “the colt of a donkey.”
John repeats Zechariah’s words “will look on” and “the One they have pierced.”
John says people “cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts”; Isaiah says “be ever seeing, but never perceiving.”
John repeats Psalms as the crowd shouts: “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord”.
